    Our Home · Our Source

    From the Heart of Gilgit-Baltistan

    Gilgit-Baltistan, in the far north of Pakistan, is where three of the world’s great mountain ranges meet — the Karakoram, the Himalayas and the Hindu Kush. Between snow-covered peaks like Rakaposhi and the turquoise waters of the Hunza River lie terraced orchards and small family farms, where almonds, walnuts and apricots have been grown for generations. Long sunny days, cold mountain nights and pure glacial water give this fruit its natural sweetness, rich oil and deep flavour — a taste you simply cannot get from the plains.

    High Valleys & Orchards

    Hunza, Nagar, Gilgit and Skardu are famous across Pakistan for their apricot orchards, walnut trees and almond groves, tended by local farming families.

    Pure Glacial Water

    Orchards here are watered by snowmelt and glacial streams. That clean, mineral-rich water and the thin mountain air help the kernels grow full, sweet and naturally crunchy.

    Sun, Patience & Hands

    Apricots are dried slowly under the mountain sun, while badam and akhrot are hand-sorted piece by piece — no shortcuts, so only the best reaches your pack.

    We source directly from Gilgit-Baltistan ourselves — no middlemen — so what grows in those valleys is exactly what arrives at your door.
